item.title: Trump’s ‘Morally Binding’ AI ‘Accord,’ the Rise of AI Agents, and Extremists on the Ballot
item.description: This week on “Uncanny Valley,” we discuss the voluntary AI safety agreement tech executives signed, AI agents for normies, and extremist candidates running for office in the US midterms.

item.title: Trump’s AI Safety ‘Accord’ Is a Fancy Pinky-Swear
item.description: Six major AI companies signed a voluntary agreement with the White House this week vowing to implement safeguards. It’s unclear how much that matters.

item.title: The Battle to Be Your Personal AI Agent Is Here
item.description: OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse are vying to be your AI agent of choice. I've tried both—and I suspect you will too.

item.title: There Are Plenty of Reasons to Be Concerned About Bioweapons Development—Even Without AI
item.description: In her new book on biological warfare, Annie Jacobsen didn’t even discuss AI because scientists can already warp Mother Nature to create extinction-level events.

item.title: OpenAI Gets Sued Over the Hugging Face Hack
item.description: A nonprofit in California is doing what Hugging Face has not—attempting to hold OpenAI legally accountable for the actions of its agents.

item.title: Anthropic Says It Discovered a Crispr-Like System. Now What?
item.description: “The experiments are still in the queue. The PR is already live,” says one expert.

item.title: OpenAI’s Dots Are Always-On AI Agents—and Its Answer to Meta’s Muse
item.description: These cute agents are designed to connect to your apps and tackle multistep tasks.

item.title: OpenAI Delays Release of Latest Model Over Safety Concerns
item.description: The company said its latest Astra model would undergo more work to meet safety standards, and issued an apology for the way it handled the hacking of an Australian government website.

item.title: Timnit Gebru Believes There Is No ‘Existential Threat’ From AI
item.description: One of AI’s fiercest critics believes the doom talk is about founders making money, not saving humanity.

item.title: OpenAI Pauses Training Its Most Powerful Models After Rogue Agents Target Government
item.description: Sam Altman says the company “have not been as fast as we would have liked” at dealing with security breaches, after news of further incidents over the summer forces another temporary halt.
